releases.title: David Duong's The King of Trash Wins Two Awards at 13th San Francisco International New Concept Film Festival
releases.body:
David Duong's remarkable journey from Vietnamese boat refugee to American entrepreneur earns two honors in San Francisco, the city where his family began rebuilding their lives nearly five decades ago.

OAKLAND, Calif., Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The King of Trash, a documentary chronicling Vietnamese American entrepreneur David Duong's remarkable journey from a refugee of the Vietnam War to the founder of a successful American recycling company, won Best Documentary and Best People Choice Film at the 13th San Francisco International New Concept Film Festival. The awards were presented on November 1 at Herbst Theatre in San Francisco, recognizing a film that follows the Duong family's history of war, survival, immigration and their pursuit of the American dream across generations.

The King of Trash Wins Best Documentary and Best People Choice Film, Celebrating a Vietnamese Refugee's American Dream

David Duong dedicated the documentary and both awards to his parents, Jim Thu Tai Duong and Anh Thi Le, whose sacrifices helped the family survive the aftermath of the Vietnam War and begin again in America. Before the fall of Saigon in April 1975, his father had built one of South Vietnam's largest paper recycling businesses, earning the nickname Vua Rác, meaning "the King of Trash," which later became the film's title. The family's circumstances changed dramatically after the war, when they lost their established business and eventually made the difficult decision to leave Vietnam.

David was among 23 family members who escaped aboard a small boat, risking their lives at sea. "We almost died out there in the ocean. We had only one choice: survive," Duong recalls in the documentary. The family eventually reached a refugee camp in the Philippines before being resettled in the United States. They arrived in San Francisco in 1979, leaving behind the home and livelihood they had known in Vietnam.

Sixteen family members shared two small studio apartments in San Francisco's Tenderloin neighborhood. With little money and limited English, they returned to the recycling trade their father had established in Vietnam, collecting cardboard, newspapers, aluminum cans and other discarded materials to support themselves. David attended school during the day and often spent his evenings collecting recyclables, sometimes working until midnight. The income helped cover the family's expenses as they learned to make a living in their new country.

In 1992, after years working in the recycling industry, David Duong founded California Waste Solutions in Oakland. The company expanded into residential and commercial recycling collection, materials processing and municipal services, eventually serving hundreds of thousands of customers in Oakland and San José. His business interests later extended to Vietnam, where he invested in environmental infrastructure through Vietnam Waste Solutions, including the Da Phuoc Integrated Waste Management Facility serving the Ho Chi Minh City region.

Directed by filmmaker Errol Webber, the 72-minute documentary follows the family's history across three generations. It also recounts the discrimination David says he experienced as a Vietnamese immigrant, the challenges he faced establishing a business in a competitive American industry, and the contributions of relatives who worked alongside him. Their accounts tell a broader story of a family that survived war, found refuge in America and gradually built a future through the work they knew.

From Collecting Recyclables to Building California Waste Solutions

In 1983, the Duong family established CoGiDo Paper Corporation with approximately $700 and a used truck. After several years collecting and selling recyclable materials in San Francisco, they began developing a more established recycling operation in the Bay Area. Family members worked together to expand the business, acquire additional equipment and build relationships with commercial customers.

CoGiDo continued to grow, and in 1989, the family sold the company to a larger corporation. By then, David had spent years learning the recycling industry alongside his father, gaining experience in collecting and processing materials, managing daily operations and working with customers. He later decided to establish a company capable of competing for larger commercial and municipal recycling contracts.

In 1992, David founded California Waste Solutions in Oakland with eight used trucks. Establishing the company required financing equipment, hiring employees, developing facilities and competing against established waste management operators. As he recounts in the documentary, he also faced discrimination and difficulties gaining acceptance as an immigrant business owner.

In 1993, California Waste Solutions secured its first municipal franchise contract with the City of Oakland. The company continued expanding its collection and processing operations over the following decades, investing in recycling facilities, vehicles and equipment as it developed services for communities in Oakland and San José.

Today, California Waste Solutions serves more than 343,000 customers in Oakland and San José, providing residential and commercial recycling collection, materials processing and resource recovery services. From its beginnings with eight used trucks in 1992, the company has expanded into one of the Bay Area's established recycling service providers, operating collection fleets and processing facilities across Northern California.

California Waste Solutions remains a family-owned business, with David Duong's sons, Michael, Johnny and Danny Duong, and his siblings, Kristina and Victor Duong, involved in the company's management and operations. Their involvement continues a family history in recycling that began with Jim Thu Tai Duong in South Vietnam and has now extended across three generations.

Over the decades, the family's work has grown from collecting and selling recyclable materials on the streets of San Francisco to operating municipal recycling services in Oakland and San José. Today, California Waste Solutions manages collection fleets, processing facilities and recycling programs serving hundreds of thousands of customers, while the next generation takes on responsibilities in the business their family spent decades building.

Environmental Investments in Vietnam

Decades after leaving Vietnam as a refugee, David Duong returned to invest in the country's environmental infrastructure. Through Vietnam Waste Solutions, he developed the Da Phuoc Integrated Waste Management Facility near Ho Chi Minh City, a major waste treatment complex spanning more than 300 acres and handling thousands of tons of municipal waste daily.

The facility uses modern waste management systems, including engineered landfills, wastewater treatment, landfill gas recovery and environmental monitoring. Building on those operations, Vietnam Waste Solutions is pursuing more than $500 million in new investment for a proposed waste-to-energy plant designed to process 3,000 tons of waste daily and generate 60 megawatts of electricity. The project remains subject to regulatory approvals.

David is also pursuing the Long An Green Environmental Technology Park, a proposed development intended to expand Vietnam's waste treatment and resource recovery infrastructure.

His investments brought him back to the country where his father had established a recycling business before the Vietnam War. The King of Trash follows this period of his career, connecting the family's beginnings in Vietnam with the environmental businesses David later built in the United States and his return to invest in his homeland.

Community Involvement and Family Leadership

Beyond his business career, David Duong has remained active in Vietnamese American communities, supporting education, charitable causes and opportunities for immigrant entrepreneurs. Through California Waste Solutions and partnerships with community organizations, his family has contributed to local schools, fundraising programs and initiatives benefiting families in the United States and Vietnam.

David has also worked to strengthen connections within the Vietnamese American business community through the Vietnamese American Business Association (VABA), supporting entrepreneurship, mentorship and opportunities for younger business owners to connect with experienced leaders and investors.

The family's commitment to business and community involvement continues through the next generation. David's sons, Michael, Johnny and Danny Duong, along with his siblings, Kristina and Victor Duong, have taken on responsibilities within the family's businesses and participated in community initiatives.

The King of Trash also gives voice to different generations of the Duong family, from those who experienced the Vietnam War and refugee resettlement to those who grew up in America and later became involved in the family businesses. Their accounts offer a personal perspective on how the family's circumstances changed over the decades and how the work begun by their parents and grandparents continues today.

For David, preserving that history was one of the reasons for making the documentary. By dedicating the film and its awards to Jim Thu Tai Duong and Anh Thi Le, he recognized the parents whose decisions and sacrifices made it possible for their children to build new lives in America.

Nationwide Screenings and Film Festival Recognition

The King of Trash has been presented to audiences across the United States through a series of screening events in California, Texas, Florida and Washington, D.C.

According to the film's organizers, 12 screening events have drawn a combined attendance of more than 5,000 people. The documentary has been shown in San José, Oakland, Sacramento, Orange County, Dallas, Houston, Orlando and Washington, D.C., as well as at additional Bay Area screenings in Hayward, Dublin and Emeryville.

The film was also selected for the 2026 Red Rock Film Festival in Utah, where it was included in the festival's September program.

Director Errol Webber previously worked as a cinematographer on Music by Prudence, which won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Short Subject in 2010. For The King of Trash, he worked with David Duong and his family to recount their history from the years surrounding the fall of Saigon to their resettlement in America and the businesses established in the decades that followed.

The documentary uses historical footage, family accounts and scenes filmed in Vietnam to recount events spanning more than half a century. It includes the recollections of David and other relatives, including Victor and Kristina Duong, whose experiences help explain how the family's history has been understood by successive generations.

The 13th San Francisco International New Concept Film Festival took place from October 25 through November 1, 2026, concluding with its awards ceremony at Herbst Theatre in San Francisco. Established in 2010 and first held in 2014, the festival recognizes independent filmmaking and encourages international exchange through cinema. According to its official 2026 program, the event received 110 film entries from countries and regions around the world.

The awards ceremony brought The King of Trash back to the city where the Duong family first settled in the United States. Nearly five decades after arriving in San Francisco as refugees, their experiences became the subject of a documentary recognized with two festival awards. The film's title also preserves the nickname once given to David's father, whose recycling business in Vietnam provided the knowledge the family would later rely upon in America.

Following its U.S. screenings and festival recognition, the production team is in discussions with streaming platforms regarding wider distribution. Distribution partners and release dates will be announced once agreements are finalized.

For the official trailer, media information and future screening announcements, visit www.thekingoftrash.us.

About The King of Trash

The King of Trash is a 72-minute documentary directed by Errol Webber that chronicles the life of Vietnamese American entrepreneur David Duong and his family's pursuit of the American dream. The film follows their escape from Vietnam after the war, their years as refugees and their efforts to rebuild their lives in San Francisco, where they began collecting recyclables to support themselves. It also recounts the founding of California Waste Solutions, David's later environmental investments in Vietnam and the experiences of three generations of a family whose history spans two countries.

Official website: https://www.thekingoftrash.us/

Trailer and media information: https://www.thekingoftrash.us/media

About California Waste Solutions

Founded in Oakland in 1992 by David Duong, California Waste Solutions is a family-owned recycling and environmental services company serving Oakland and San José. The company provides residential and commercial recycling collection, materials processing and resource recovery services. According to company figures, its operations serve more than 343,000 customers in Northern California.

Official website: https://www.calwaste.com/

About the San Francisco International New Concept Film Festival

The San Francisco International New Concept Film Festival is an independent international film festival established in 2010, with its first edition held in 2014. The festival showcases films across multiple genres, recognizes independent filmmakers and encourages cultural exchange through cinema. Its 13th annual edition took place October 25 through November 1, 2026, concluding with an awards ceremony at Herbst Theatre in San Francisco.

Official website: https://www.sfnewfilms.com/

releases.title: L.A. Film School Honors Emmy Award-Winning Producer Lane Cheek Through the Spotlight Academy
releases.body:
Emmy-winning producer brings acclaimed productions to life and advocates for environmental awareness.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Los Angeles Film School is proud to recognize 2010 Film graduate Lane Cheek as one of four inductees into its Spotlight Academy for 2026. An Emmy Award-winning film and television executive producer, Cheek has built a career spanning major studios and networks while championing creative collaboration and opportunities for fellow filmmakers.

Cheek's career began with on-set and art department roles before she transitioned into producing, working on projects for 20th Century Fox, ABC/Disney, AMC+ and Warner Bros. Her credits include popular series such as The Vampire Diaries, The Originals, Halt and Catch Fire and Modern Family.

In addition to her production work, Cheek founded Cheeky Consulting in 2020 to support brand development, production strategy and creative projects. She has also produced environmental initiatives, including the documentary Our Planet 360, which explores the human impact on shark populations and the importance of ocean conservation.

Cheek's journey reflects the value of perseverance, hands-on experience and a commitment to bringing stories to life. Through her work as a producer and consultant, she continues to contribute to the entertainment industry while creating opportunities for creative professionals to develop their skills and pursue their ambitions. Her induction into the Spotlight Academy celebrates her professional achievements, environmental advocacy and dedication to the creative community.

About The Spotlight Academy

The Spotlight Academy pays tribute to the heart, the creative and the dedicated among The Los Angeles Film School's alumni. Each year, Academy Inductees are honored for their unyielding commitment to excellence in their professional career and selfless contribution of time and connection to our students and community. It is with great privilege we shine a spotlight on these inspirational and exceptional individuals.

To learn more about the Spotlight Academy and its inductees, visit lafilm.edu/alumni/the-spotlight-academy.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Scientology Media Productions' Signature Performances documentary Mark Isham: The Voice Within has earned a nomination for a 2026 Hollywood Music in Media Award (HMMA) in the Music Documentary – Special Program category.

Scientology Network’s Mark Isham: The Voice Within earns a 2026 Hollywood Music in Media Award nomination.

This year's nominees feature documentaries on some of the most influential artists in music, including Mark Isham: The Voice Within, Man on the Run (Paul McCartney), Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger, The Rise of the Red Hot Chili Peppers: Our Brother, Hillel, Linda Perry: Let It Die Here and Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special (Miley Cyrus). Also nominated is 40 Watts From Nowhere.

The documentary takes viewers inside the creative world of Grammy and Emmy-winning composer and trumpeter Mark Isham, whose career spans more than four decades and over 400 film and television projects. Tracing his evolution from jazz and electronic music pioneer to acclaimed Hollywood composer, the film follows Isham as he brings together an extraordinary ensemble of musicians, including drummer Vinnie Colaiuta, guitarist Nels Cline, bassist Kaveh Rastegar, vocalist Ayo Awosika and the Orchid Quartet, to blend free-form jazz with electronica for At the Carousel Club, his first new album in 15 years.

"I'm so delighted and honored to have had my creative process documented with such quality by a talented team. It's a very special and unique opportunity to share my art, since the purpose of my art is ultimately to communicate at a very high aesthetic level," said Mark Isham.

Now in its 17th year, the Hollywood Music in Media Awards honors outstanding music across film, television, documentaries, video games, trailers, commercials and other visual media. Winners will be announced at the 17th annual HMMA ceremony on November 18, 2026.

Mark Isham: The Voice Within premiered October 11 on Scientology Network and is now available to watch on demand at scientology.tv/markisham.

Scientology Network debuted on March 12, 2018, launched by David Miscavige, ecclesiastical leader of the Scientology religion. Since then, Scientology Network has been viewed in over 240 countries and territories worldwide in 17 languages. Satisfying the curiosity of people about Scientology, the network takes viewers across six continents, spotlighting the everyday lives of Scientologists, showing the Church as a global organization and presenting its Social Betterment programs that have touched the lives of millions worldwide. The network also showcases documentaries by independent filmmakers who represent a cross section of cultures and faiths, but share a common purpose of uplifting communities. Scientology Network's innovative content has been recognized with more than 175 industry awards, including Tellys, Communitas and Hermes Creative Awards.

Broadcast from Scientology Media Productions, the Church's global media center in Los Angeles, Scientology Network is available on DIRECTV Channel 320, DIRECTV STREAM and AT&T U-verse and can be streamed at scientology.tv, on mobile apps and via the Roku, Amazon Fire and Apple TV platforms.

releases.title: Music or Magic? bubly™ Brings Michael Bublé and The Elf on the Shelf® Together to Settle When the Holiday Season Really Begins
releases.body:
New research from bubly reveals when Canadians start celebrating and the traditions that signal the holiday season has arrived

Key Facts

  • bubly™ sparkling water beverage has launched a new holiday partnership with global superstar Michael Bublé and The Elf on the Shelf® Santaverse to bring Canadians festive content and playful holiday moments throughout the season.
  • Half of Canadians aged 18-34 say they start celebrating the holidays before December 1.
  • 90% of Canadians say family traditions help make the holiday season magical.
  • 70% of Canadians include holiday music among their holiday traditions.
  • From November 3-9, Canadians can vote through bubly Canada's Instagram and TikTok channels (@bublysparklingca) on what officially signals the start of the holiday season: music or magic.

MISSISSAUGA, ON, Nov. 3, 2026 /CNW/ -- bubly, Canada's No. 1 sparkling beverage brand, is teaming up with GRAMMY ® Award-winning, multi-platinum entertainer Michael Bublé and The Elf on the Shelf® Santaverse to ask Canadians what officially signals the start of the holiday season: the music or the magic? Michael Bublé and The Elf on the Shelf ® are playfully representing each side of the debate. The playful debate kicks off a broader holiday partnership designed to bring a little more fun and bubly spirit to the holiday season.

New research commissioned by bubly suggests that the holiday countdown may begin earlier than most people think. Half of Canadians aged 18-34 say they start celebrating before December 1, compared to 39 per cent who say their holiday celebrations begin in December. Starting the holiday season before December 1 is especially common among respondents in Atlantic Canada (49 per cent) and Saskatchewan and Manitoba (47 per cent).

For many, the holidays begin to feel real when the familiar sights of the season start to appear. Decorating a Christmas tree or hanging decorations (16 per cent) and spotting holiday lights appearing around the neighbourhood (15 per cent) were the moments most likely to bring a smile and signal that the season had begun. Food and drinks are also part of bringing holiday gatherings to life. Among Canadians who include sparkling water in their holiday celebrations, more than half (51 per cent) say they enjoy bubly.

bubly Announces Holiday Partnership with GRAMMY® Award-winning global superstar Michael Bublé and The Elf on the Shelf ® Santaverse

The holiday kickoff debate is just the beginning. Throughout the season, bubly, Michael Bublé and The Elf on the Shelf ® will come together for a series of festive content and playful holiday moments designed to help Canadians crack a smile. From music to magic, the collaboration celebrates the traditions and moments that make the season feel special, with bubly along for the celebration.

"bubly is all about creating moments that crack a smile, and the holidays are full of them. Whether it's gathering with family and friends over food and drinks or celebrating favourite traditions, teaming up with Michael Bublé and The Elf on the Shelf felt like a fun way to celebrate traditions that get Canadians into the holiday spirit and let them have a say in what officially kicks off the season," says Sean Cauterman, Marketing Director, Growth Brands, PepsiCo Canada.

How Can Canadians Vote in the bubly Music vs. Magic Holiday Debate?

Inspired by the survey findings, bubly, part of PepsiCo Canada's food and beverage portfolio, along with Michael Bublé and The Elf on the Shelf ® Santaverse are inviting Canadians to weigh in on one festive question. Does the season begin with the music or the magic? With Michael representing music and The Elf on the Shelf ® representing magic, Canadians can choose a side.

From November 3–8, Canadians can visit bubly Canada's Instagram and TikTok channels (@bublysparklingca) to cast their vote on what they believe officially signals the start of the holiday season. Voting runs through November 9, when bubly will reveal the results and settle the holiday debate.

"For me, the holidays start when the music does, but apparently The Scout Elf has other ideas.  So, this year, bubly is helping us settle the debate once and for all, and we're letting Canada decide," says Michael Bublé.

On the other side of the holiday debate, The Elf on the Shelf ® is making the case for magic.

"The Elf on the Shelf has been delighting Canadian families for years, so we're thrilled to team up with bubly and Michael Bublé this holiday season. For many Canadians, the Scout Elf's return and the first notes of Michael's holiday music both signal that the season has officially begun, and everyone seems to have an opinion on which comes first! We love that bubly is giving Canadians a fun way to join in the debate and celebrate the magic of the season," says Christa Pitts, co-CEO, The Lumistella Company.

The holiday debate doesn't end with the vote. Canadians can follow @bublysparklingca on Instagram and TikTok throughout the season for more from bubly, Michael Bublé and The Elf on the Shelf ®.

About the Research:

bubly commissioned Angus Reid to conduct an online survey from October 1-6, 2026, among 1,006 Canadian adults aged 18 and older who are members of the Angus Reid Forum. Respondents were required to observe at least one year-end holiday, including Christmas, Hanukkah, Diwali, Kwanzaa or New Year's Eve, and have established holiday traditions within their family. The survey was conducted in English and French. Results are accurate within plus or minus 3.1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20.

About bubly™

bubly is a sparkling water beverage brand from PepsiCo Canada known for its playful personality and colourful, flavour-forward products. Available in 13 flavours across Canada, bubly sparkling water beverage has zero sugar, zero calories, and no artificial flavours or sweeteners. With the launch of bubly POP™ soda, the brand expands into a new category for the first time. Follow @bublysparklingca on Instagram and TikTok.

About PepsiCo

PepsiCo products are enjoyed by consumers more than one billion times a day in more than 200 countries and territories around the world. PepsiCo generated nearly $94 billion in net revenue in 2025, driven by a complementary beverage and convenient foods portfolio that includes Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola, Mountain Dew, Quaker, and SodaStream. PepsiCo's product portfolio includes a wide range of enjoyable foods and drinks, including many iconic brands that generate more than $1 billion each in estimated annual retail sales. Guiding PepsiCo is our vision to Be the Global Leader in Beverages and Convenient Foods by Winning with pep+ (PepsiCo Positive). pep+ is our strategic end-to-end transformation that places sustainability at the center of our business strategy, seeking to drive growth and build a stronger, more resilient future for PepsiCo and the communities where we operate. For more information, visit www.pepsico.ca, and follow on X (Twitter), Instagram, Facebook and Linkedin @PepsiCo.

About The Lumistella Company 

CCA and B, LLC d/b/a The Lumistella Company is the company behind Santaverse®, the official source for the stories of the enchanted world of Santa Claus. Family-owned and women-led since 2005, the company's portfolio includes a number of iconic Christmas brands, including: The Elf on the Shelf, Elf Pets and Elf Mates. As a global company operating in 33 countries, on 6 continents with 100+ licensees, our purpose is to make joyful family moments possible around the world. To learn more about The Lumistella Company, please visit https://lumistella.com/.

About Michael Bublé 

Michael Bublé has sold more than 75 million albums worldwide over the course of his extraordinary career and has enjoyed enormous success as one of the top touring artists of all time. With a career that includes 5 GRAMMYs®,15 JUNO Awards, a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame and Canada's Walk of Fame, 6 multi-platinum albums, and over 14 billion global streams, Michael has spent the past two decades deeply committed to not only keep the flames of the Great American Songbook alive and well - to not only breathe new life into them - but to bring his singular style, vocal power, and passion to timeless tunes that he loves. He released his self-titled debut album on Reprise Records in 2003, followed by a series of multi-platinum, #1 albums including Call Me Irresponsible (2007), Crazy Love (2009), To Be Loved (2013), Love (2018), and Christmas (2011). Michael's 11th studio album HIGHER (2022) marked his 9th Top 10 on Billboard's Top Album Sales Chart and 7th consecutive studio album to debut in the Top 3. Known for his world-class showmanship and spectacular concert production, he has performed sold out shows in over 30 countries. With unstoppable talent, energy and a voice that is equally at home singing standards, pop, swing, jazz, R&B, and comedy, Michael takes his audiences on a special journey every night - singing his heart out, serenading them with beautiful love songs, making them laugh, cry, and dance - to give them an evening they will never forget. In September 2024, Michael joined the powerhouse coaching panel on NBC's The Voice, taking home back-to-back wins on both Seasons 26 and 27. The two-time champion then returned for Season 28 in 2025, which marked a historic, third consecutive season as a coach on the show.

Miami's Favorite Holiday Tradition Marks Its Fourth Season With Light Up the Night, an Hourly Light and Music Spectacular Along the Mile-Long Tinsel Trail, Plus Duck Discovery, Holiday Harmonies Choir Nights, Six Themed Holiday Worlds, More Than 50 Unlimited Carnival Rides, and Food and Drinks From Miami's Favorite Local Vendors

MIAMI, Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- For generations of South Florida families, the first sign of Christmas was the glow of lights through the trees at Tropical Park, spotted from the back seat on the drive down the Palmetto Expressway. This season, Christmas Wonderland at Tropical Park carries that hometown tradition into its fourth year from Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, through Sunday, Jan. 3, 2027. Produced by Loud And Live, the Miami-based entertainment company behind many of the region's large-scale events, the 14-acre celebration debuts the 230-foot America 250 Wheel, a classic European-style Christmas market, and new experiences for families, all set along a mile of lights synchronized to music.

Miami's Favorite Holiday Tradition Marks It's Fourth Season. Christmas Wonderland Returns To Tropical Park Nov. 12th.

Christmas Wonderland pairs the nostalgia Miami's grown-ups remember with a polished, modern holiday night out built for today's families, couples and friends. Guests will find immersive themed worlds designed by award-winning creative teams, more than 50 unlimited carnival rides, hundreds of photo moments, craft cocktails and coquito, seasonal brews, and a lineup of Miami's favorite local food vendors. Every ride, show, and attraction is included with a single admission ticket.

"Miami grew up celebrating Christmas at Tropical Park, and our job is to give the next generation a version of that tradition worth passing down," said Tony Albelo, President of Loud And Live Events. "This year we invested in the details guests feel the moment they walk in, from a light show choreographed to music every hour, to a Christmas market inspired by the fabulous holiday markets of Europe. It is the kind of night families, couples, and friends will want to make part of their season every year."

LIGHT UP THE NIGHT: A MILE OF LIGHTS, CHOREOGRAPHED TO MUSIC

At the heart of Christmas Wonderland is Tinsel Trail, a mile of lights that winds through all six of the park's holiday worlds. What drivers glimpse from the Palmetto is only a preview. Every hour on the hour, the entire mile-long trail comes together for Light Up the Night, a synchronized light and music spectacular in which every archway, display, and installation along the route moves in time to a holiday soundtrack. The show travels through the themes of the trail, from the Miami color of HoliDade to the frosty hush of Arctic Delight, and builds to a parkwide finale in the European-style new marketplace.

Guests will reach for their phones, and many will find themselves lowering them to take in the moment with the people beside them. Light Up the Night is included with admission and runs every hour, every night of the season.

NEW FOR 2026

  • America 250 Wheel: Rising 230 feet above Tropical Park, the America 250 Wheel is billed as the world's largest portable observation wheel and was built to celebrate the nation's 250th anniversary. Each of its 45 gondolas honors one of the 45 U.S. presidents and shares historical facts with riders, while views from the top stretch up to 14 miles. The 700,000-pound wheel arrives on 11 tractor-trailers. Rides are included with paid admission.



  • Christmas Marketplace: The Christmas Marketplace makes its debut as a brand-new addition to Tinsel Trail, bringing the spirit of Europe's bespoke Christmas markets to Tropical Park. Twinkling chalets and picturesque photo moments surround the park's towering Christmas tree, where artisans and local Miami vendors offer holiday classics like handcrafted ornaments and seasonal treats. Guests can warm up and get cozy with hot cocoa from a toppings bar and spiced cider, roasted nuts, and an array of delicatessen delights, all while enjoying classic Christmas carols and visits from St. Nicholas.



  • Duck Discovery: Complimentary for children 12 and younger, this parkwide hunt follows a flock of 24 festive rubber ducks that have waddled away from the North Pole. Kids pick up a Duck Passport at the entrance, register at the Duck Depot, and search Tinsel Trail for the four to five varieties hidden each night, earning a dated stamp for every new find. Collect 10 different ducks to earn a four-pack of tickets for a return visit, or find all 24 to win a grand prize for the 2027 season. A daily "Today's Flock" sign at the entrance and on social media shows which ducks are out each night.



  • Holiday Harmonies: On Choir Nights, Dec. 1, 8, and 15, local choirs fill the park with carols, and each evening closes with a song the whole crowd sings together.



  • Santa's Enchanted Forest Memory Lane: A tribute along Tinsel Trail to the holiday tradition South Florida families grew up with at Tropical Park, Memory Lane brings back original set pieces, classic photo spots including Surfin' Santa, and the signature jingle generations of Miamians still know by heart.

SIX THEMED HOLIDAY WORLDS

Tinsel Trail connects six themed worlds, each with its own look, photo moments, and surprises:

HoliDade, presented by Estrella Insurance: A tribute to the people, culture, and neighborhoods of Miami-Dade County, with more than 12 photo installations designed by award-winning Moyano Productions, the creative team behind the Museum of Ice Cream. Highlights include the Gingerbread Lifeguard Stand, a sugar-frosted nod to Miami Beach, and the Toy Factoria, a twinkling ode to Hialeah.

Town Square: A storybook hometown setting with twinkling lights, festive storefronts, and classic holiday décor, plus Tony's Tree Farm and a vintage Christmas truck ready for its close-up.

Sweet Street, presented by Amanda Demanda: Sweet Street transforms into a vibrant landscape of candy canes, gingerbread, and holiday confections. The themed area features whimsical décor and family-friendly photo moments, with on-site safety reminders and holiday tips from this year's returning sponsor, Amanda Demanda, underscoring the firm's commitment to community well-being during the season.

Toy Town: Oversized toys, Santa's Elf Brigade, kid-sized rides including the Kids Wheel, and a Letters to Santa station where children can send their wishes to the North Pole.

Arctic Delight: Guests step through a wall of snow into a frosty winter scene. Adults can raise a glass at Nelson's Nightcap Bar, presented by XXL Wines, pouring wine, Champagne, seasonal cocktails, and ready-to-drink cans.

Santa's Village: At the end of the trail, Santa welcomes guests to the North Pole among the reindeer stables and busy elf workshops. Professional commemorative photos with Santa are available for an additional fee, with advance booking recommended.

RIDES, FOOD, AND DRINK

Beyond the trail, The Magnificent Midway delivers more than 50 rides, from three roller coasters and high-energy thrill rides to family favorites such as the carousel and bumper cars, all included with admission.

Food and drink are part of the night. Some of South Florida's favorite food trucks and local vendors serve holiday sweets, local specialties, and carnival classics, while festive bars pour coquito, craft cocktails, and seasonal beverages throughout the park. XXL Wines presents Nelson's Nightcap Bar in Arctic Delight, pouring wine, Champagne, ready-to-drink mixed drinks, and more, while Cervecería La Tropical returns as the official beer partner with refreshing seasonal brews.

Christmas Wonderland also welcomes back several valued partners, including FPL, Presenting Partner of the Opening Ceremony; Ford, Official Truck Partner; Goya; Club Travalia and Florida Blue, whose continued support helps bring the holiday magic to life.

CALGARY, AB, Nov. 2, 2026 /CNW/ -- Today, Cadillac Fairview (CF) unveiled its 2026 holiday programming across Calgary. Beginning this month, CF will bring the magic of the season as the holidays really are better in real life where guests come together to enjoy live holiday music, visits with Santa and Mrs. Claus, and festive gift inspiration for the whole family at CF Chinook Centre and CF Market Mall.

"The most memorable moments of the season are the ones we share together, the excitement of a child meeting Santa for the first time, finding the perfect gift, or simply enjoying the festive atmosphere with family and friends," said Andrea Nickel, Senior Director, Experience, Design & Delivery at Cadillac Fairview. "Our holiday programming reflects our commitment to creating welcoming spaces where Canadians can gather and celebrate in ways that feel meaningful to them."

Festive Highlights Across Calgary

Santa Visits: A Cherished Tradition (Beginning November 13)

Santa returns to select CF shopping centres from Friday, November 13 to Wednesday, December 23. CF Insiders receive early ticket access starting Monday, November 2, with general public online booking opening Tuesday, November 3. This year, guests will step inside Santa's Mailroom, a brand-new North Pole set for their visit and photo with Santa and it also features an exterior holiday themed photo opp area where visitors can take their own photo and kids can write and leave their letters to Santa. Pre-booked five-minute sessions cost $17.50 and include five digital photos. Guests booking Santa visits at CF Chinook Centre will enjoy LEGO® minibuild giveaways on select days, courtesy of the LEGO Group.

In partnership with the Autism Alliance of Canada, Sensitive Santa sessions will offer a quieter, lower-sensory environment for children with sensory needs. Walk-up visits will be available on-site as schedule permits. Reservations can be made at shops.cadillacfairview.com.

The Christmas Court Live Performance Series at CF Chinook Centre (Beginning November 13)

Beginning Friday, November 13, CF Chinook Centre will host its exciting Christmas Court Series on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays throughout the season. The series brings a rotating lineup of must-see local entertainment, including acoustic musicians, seasonal vocalists, DJs and ballet performances featuring the Nutcracker and Sugar Plum Fairies, performing against the backdrop of the magical holiday décor.

Weekend Strolls with Mrs. Claus at CF Market Mall (Beginning November 14)

Mrs. Claus will be taking festive strolls around CF Market Mall on weekends from Saturday, November 14 to Sunday, December 20, between 12:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. Accompanied by CF Brand Ambassadors, she will greet families, hand out candy canes, and share special retailer perks.

Discover Holiday Gift Inspiration with CF 

Shop the Gift Guide (Beginning November 16)

Launching just in time for Black Friday, CF's digital Shop the Gift guide takes the guesswork out of holiday shopping. Curated specifically for each CF property, the interactive guide features top holiday picks across seven easy-to-browse categories: Home Décor & Festive Touches, Jewellery & Sparkle, Stocking Stuffers, Fashion & Accessories, Toys for All Ages, Games & Family Fun, and In-Property Experiences. Shoppers can explore their local centre's guide at shops.cadillacfairview.com.

Promotions & Extended Holiday Hours 

CF SHOP! card® Perks & Promotions (November 19)

The CF SHOP! card offers a convenient gifting option available at Guest Services, online at cfshopcard.ca, or at self-serve kiosks located across major CF properties including CF Chinook Centre.

Ahead of Black Friday on Thursday, November 19, guests who purchase $250 in CF SHOP! cards in person at Guest Services will receive a $25 promotional bonus card (up to a maximum of $200 in bonus cards per person, while supplies last).

To give shoppers extra time to make the most of the season, CF shopping centres are also extending their operational hours, with tailored schedules varying by property to best serve local communities. For complete holiday shopping hours, event schedules, booking details, and centre-specific programming, visit shops.cadillacfairview.com.

Cadillac Fairview (CF) is one of the largest owners, operators, investors and developers of best-in-class office, retail, multi-family residential, industrial and mixed-use properties in Canada. NEW YORK, Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- From Chevy Chase's Vacation to Ryan Reynolds' Van Wilder, National Lampoon has helped define American comedy for generations. Now, the iconic brand is partnering with Rip Micheals Entertainment and Eugene Parker's 5120 Entertainment for an expansion spanning arena events, films, original series and a new comedy channel, alongside a revenue platform designed to help comedians keep earning from their work.
releases.title: From Chevy Chase and Ryan Reynolds to Sold-Out Arenas: National Lampoon Launches Its Next Chapter With 'Wild 'N Out Live!' Tour Creator and Producer Rip Micheals and 5120 Entertainment
releases.body:
A new film starring Alec Baldwin and Nick Cannon. A December comedy series featuring Na'im Lynn and guest-starring Kevin Hart. A Barclays Center event followed by a tour slated for late spring 2027. And Rip Micheals' first stand-up special: no stage—all crowd.

NEW YORK, Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- From Chevy Chase's Vacation to Ryan Reynolds' Van Wilder, National Lampoon has helped define American comedy for generations. Now, the iconic brand is partnering with Rip Micheals Entertainment and Eugene Parker's 5120 Entertainment for an expansion spanning arena events, films, original series and a new comedy channel, alongside a revenue platform designed to help comedians keep earning from their work.

The announced slate includes National Lampoon's Hollywood Hustle, starring Alec Baldwin and Nick Cannon, planned for early 2027, and a comedy vertical series featuring Na'im Lynn, with Kevin Hart guest-starring alongside an ensemble cast, slated for December 2026.

The live entertainment expansion arrives at Barclays Center in Brooklyn on December 17, while Rip Micheals' In the Crowd Work premieres November 26, putting Micheals directly among the audience with a distinctive premise: no stage—all crowd.

These projects introduce the ambitions behind National Lampoon Presents, the new banner launching December 2, 2026.

FROM TELEVISION TO SOLD-OUT ARENAS

The partnership pairs more than five decades of National Lampoon comedy heritage with the live entertainment experience of Rip Micheals, creator and producer of the Wild 'N Out Live! tour, April Fools Comedy Jam and other large-scale comedy productions.

Micheals took Wild 'N Out from television to sold-out venues nationwide across four tours, reaching more than 1.5 million fans in over 100 cities. Its touring achievements include a Pollstar record for staging two shows in two different markets on the same night.

The partners' strategy connects live events that build audiences with original programming that extends their reach, while the new channel and album revenue platform create additional earning opportunities for performers.

BARCLAYS CENTER: COMEDY'S LEGACY MEETS ITS NEXT GENERATION

On December 17, 2026, Barclays Center in Brooklyn will bring together comedy legends associated with National Lampoon's legacy and some of the hottest performers from Rip Micheals's sold-out arena tours.

Celebrating National Lampoon's decades-long contribution to comedy, the event will connect generations of performers and audiences on one arena stage. Participating performers and additional event details will be announced separately, with a tour slated to launch in late spring 2027.

NO STAGE. ALL CROWD.

Premiering November 26, 2026, In the Crowd Work is Rip Micheals' first stand-up special, placing him directly among the audience rather than on a stage.

The audience becomes the center of the performance, with Micheals building the special around his interactions with the people surrounding him. The format brings viewers into the exchange between comedian and crowd.

STAR-DRIVEN FILMS AND ORIGINAL COMEDY

The planned early-2027 film slate includes Hollywood Hustle, starring Alec Baldwin and Nick Cannon, alongside new films from 5120 Entertainment, with additional movie content expected as early as January.

Slated for December 2026, the new comedy vertical series featuring Na'im Lynn and guest-starring Kevin Hart adds short-form storytelling to the lineup, alongside an ensemble cast. Additional programming includes Na'im Lynn's My Stand-Up Series.

The slate connects established names and emerging voices across live performance, stand-up, film and digital series.

A NEW HOME FOR COMEDY—AND ONGOING INCOME FOR COMEDIANS

The partners are also launching a new comedy channel that will produce comedy specials, creating a destination for original stand-up and comedian-led programming.

A companion revenue platform is designed to give comedians opportunities to earn ongoing residual income from their comedy albums, extending the earning potential of their work beyond a single performance.

Short sets, roast sessions, digital radio and podcasts are also part of the broader programming plans. Together, the live events, channel and revenue platform are intended to help performers develop material, reach audiences and build lasting value from their work.

"Comedians need a home where they can put their material out, reach audiences, and earn from their work," said Rip Micheals, founder of Rip Micheals. "We took Wild 'N Out from the screen to sold-out arenas."

Beyond Wild 'N Out Live!, Micheals' production portfolio includes April Fools Comedy Jam, featuring Marlon Wayans; Fall Back in Love Comedy & Music Jam; and Urban Eats and Treats. His international production credits include UK comedy performances featuring Marlon Wayans and Eddie Griffin.

"National Lampoon has always stood for bold, original comedy that pushes boundaries and brings people together," said National Lampoon representative Jerry Daigle. "With this partnership, we're building on that legacy while creating new opportunities for comedians and introducing the brand to a new generation of audiences. Rip Micheals and 5120 Entertainment bring a strong track record in live entertainment and a shared vision for creating fresh, exciting comedy experiences. We're looking forward to what we can build together."

National Lampoon's history spans publishing, film, stage and radio. Its Radio Hour and stage production Lemmings helped launch performers including Chevy Chase, John Belushi, Bill Murray, Gilda Radner and Harold Ramis.

The partnership connects that legacy with Micheals' arena touring experience and 5120 Entertainment's film and television capabilities.

"At 5120 Entertainment, we're focused on building projects that connect talent with audiences," said Eugene Parker, CEO of 5120 Entertainment. "Our partnership with National Lampoon gives us the opportunity to bring an iconic comedy brand to new audiences and develop experiences across live events, and ultimately television, film, and digital projects. We're excited to build alongside National Lampoon and Rip Micheals Entertainment."

Further announcements will include viewing information, Barclays Center event details, tour dates, additional programming dates and information about the new channel and comedian revenue platform.

ABOUT NATIONAL LAMPOON

National Lampoon is an American comedy brand spanning film, stage, radio and publishing. Its cultural touchstones include Animal House, the Vacation franchise, National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation and Van Wilder.

ABOUT RIP MICHEALS

Founded by comedian, creator and producer Rip Micheals, Rip Micheals produces large-scale comedy, music and entertainment experiences. Micheals is the creator and producer of the Wild 'N Out Live! tour, April Fools Comedy Jam, Fall Back in Love Comedy & Music Jam and Urban Eats and Treats.

ABOUT 5120 ENTERTAINMENT

Led by CEO Eugene Parker, 5120 Entertainment develops and produces film, television and live entertainment projects. Its credits include Back on the Strip, starring Wesley Snipes, Tiffany Haddish and Kevin Hart.

LONDON, Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PRG Projects, part of global entertainment technology company PRG (Production Resource Group), today announced the opening of Project Studio, a new collaborative space in central London that expands the company's custom engineering and technology integration capabilities, bringing its technical expertise closer to the creative teams shaping the future of live entertainment.

The opening reflects PRG Projects' commitment to working alongside designers and the people behind the ideas from the earliest stages of development, providing the engineering expertise and technical resources needed to bring their visions to life. Project Studio is not a design studio, but a dedicated environment where creative teams can collaborate directly with PRG Projects' specialists to explore new technologies, overcome technical challenges and develop innovative production solutions.

Through Project Studio, creative teams have direct access to PRG Projects' expertise across concept development, budgeting, sourcing, engineering, integration, implementation, sustainability and project management. The new space builds on 25 years of experience developing and manufacturing custom audiovisual technology and integrating it with stage elements for major live productions.

Led by Frederic Opsomer, Managing Director, PRG Projects has a track record of turning ambitious creative concepts into groundbreaking technical solutions for some of the world's largest live productions. Its innovations include:

  • the custom-engineered inflatable LED spheres for Coldplay's Music of the Spheres World Tour, and the eight-meter modular LED sphere developed for Eric Prydz's Holosphere 2.0
  • the lightweight carbon-fiber SPACEFRAME system created for U2's The Joshua Tree Tour
  • INFINIFORM™, a modular scenic platform that provides designers with reusable, customizable infrastructure for dynamic stage designs, used on tours for Post Malone, The 1975, Tate McRae, and more.

Each project demonstrates the team's ability to push the boundaries of existing technology, developing custom solutions that bring creative visions to life.

"Some of the most exciting ideas in live entertainment begin with a creative vision that doesn't yet have a technical solution," said Frederic Opsomer, Managing Director of PRG Projects. "By having a presence in London, we scale what PRG Projects does best: having the entrepreneurship to say yes to bold ideas, impacting the experience of millions of concertgoers worldwide."

Project Studio is now open at 84 Marchmont Street, London WC1N 1AG, with Kahren Williams, Commercial Manager for PRG Projects, based at the location. For inquiries, contact info.projects@prg.com.

releases.title: iQIYI Launches China's First AI Film Studio in Shanghai, with Inaugural Title "Cop in Trouble" in Production
releases.body:
BEIJING, Nov. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On October 28, iQIYI, China's leading online entertainment platform, has begun the inaugural project at its newly opened AI Film Studio with the filming of internet feature film "Cop in Trouble". Located at the iQIYI Creative Center Shanghai, the AI Film Studio expands upon iQIYI's AI ecosystem integrating live-action in-studio filming with AI post-production to realize the imagination of storytellers at scale.

Fewer Constraints, Greater Creative Freedom 

Combining live studio performances with AI post-production, iQIYI reduces production timeline constraints and increases production efficiency, helping filmmakers realize their intended creative vision. For example, the studio gives filmmakers greater flexibility to develop and refine visual environments after filming, while preserving the actors' original performances.

The approximately 110-square-meter studio is equipped with multi-camera shooting capabilities, synchronized high-resolution video and audio recording, digital continuity logging, and real-time footage review. From the set, on-set footage syncs automatically to NadouPro, iQIYI's AI-powered film & TV production platform. This seamless integration gives filmmakers immediate access to nearly 30 AI models, including Seedance 2.5 and Kling 4.0, as well as hundreds of production-focused AI agents and skills to transform live-action footage by generating new visual elements.

"An actor's performance is the core of any film or series," said Liang ZHU, iQIYI Vice President and Head of Intelligent Production. "The AI studio lets directors preserve that performance while adjusting sets, lighting and costumes, makeup, and props more flexibly, opening up greater creative space for filmmakers and creative professionals alike."

Bringing the story of "Cop in Trouble" to Life

The production of the film "Cop in Trouble" puts the new capabilities to practice. "Cop in Trouble" follows Jian ZHANG, a low-ranking constable whose fame, riches and admiration begin to crack as his web of lies to take down a notorious outlaw begins to unravel. 

"Cop in Trouble" demonstrates how iQIYI's AI Film Studio combines live-action performances with AI-generated environments and visual details. On set, filmmakers capture nuanced interactions between actors, from intimate conversations to action sequences requiring precise coordination between performers and camera movement.

These live-action recordings provide rich input and key references for the AI generation process via NadouPro, particularly in terms of character appearance, performance, composition, lighting, and spatial relationships.

With the production of "Cop in Trouble" underway, the AI Film Studio marks another important step in the expansion of iQIYI's production capabilities – from traditional on-location and green-screen work to virtual production and AI-integrated filmmaking. The new facility continues the success of iQIYI's Hengdian virtual studio, which delivered production efficiency gains of over 30% to unlock a new era of high-quality, cinematic storytelling at scale.

The new AI Film Studio opens up new possibilities for emerging directors and resource-constrained teams, particularly in bringing imaginative worlds to life across all genres.

releases.title: Shenzhen Unveils APEC China 2026 Host-City Theme Song and Music Video
releases.body:
SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 1, 2026 /CNW/ -- The host-city theme song for APEC China 2026, Meet You Where Wonders Bloom (在奇迹之城遇见你), was produced by the Publicity Department of the CPC Shenzhen Municipal Committee and created by Shenzhen Media Group. Written and composed by He Muyang, Vice Chairman of the Chinese Musicians Association and a Shenzhen-based musician, the song is performed by popular singers Jane Zhang and Joseph Zeng. With its fresh, youthful pop sound, the song tells the stories of ordinary dreamers, weaving together personal aspirations, Shenzhen's remarkable development, and the broader vision of Asia-Pacific cooperation.

Released alongside the song, the music video goes beyond showcasing Shenzhen's cityscape to put people at the heart of the story. Through the experiences of people from all walks of life, particularly young people and those from overseas, it captures the energy and appeal of Shenzhen, the City of Miracles, and its warm welcome to the world. Running 4 minutes and 45 seconds, the video features 176 shots filmed across Shenzhen, with more than 100 residents appearing on screen. From location coordination and filming support to bringing participants together, the production was a citywide effort. releases.title: The King of Trash, Following David Duong's Journey From Vietnamese Refugee to Business Leader, Named Finalist at 13th San Francisco International New Concept Film Festival
releases.body:
Following 12 U.S. screening events, the documentary returns the Duong family's story to San Francisco, where they began rebuilding their lives after escaping Vietnam.

OAKLAND, Calif., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The King of Trash, a 72-minute documentary tracing David Duong and his family's journey from their escape from Vietnam by boat to rebuilding their lives in San Francisco and establishing businesses in the United States and Vietnam, has been named a finalist at the 13th San Francisco International New Concept Film Festival. Director Errol Webber and producer David Duong are scheduled to attend the November 1 red carpet and awards ceremony at Herbst Theatre in San Francisco.

The King of Trash named San Francisco film festival finalist, spotlighting David Duong's refugee-to-entrepreneur story.

The festival recognition brings the film back to the city where the Duong family arrived as refugees in 1979. Before David Duong founded California Waste Solutions, relatives shared apartments in the Tenderloin and collected discarded bottles, cardboard and paper to support the household. That period, along with the family's experiences during the Vietnam War and its subsequent return to Vietnam, forms the central story of the documentary.

"We are thrilled that the movie has been recognized by such a prestigious film festival," said California Waste Solutions Founder & CEO David Duong. "We've received tremendous feedback which has been very touching from people all over California who have said how it has impacted them in different ways. Now it's an honor to be a finalist at the San Francisco New Concept Film Festival."

The documentary has been shown at 12 screening events across the United States, drawing audiences in San Jose, Oakland, Sacramento, Orange County, Dallas, Houston, Washington, D.C., Orlando, Hayward, Dublin, San Jose, and Emeryville. Together, the 12 events have drawn more than 5,000 attendees, bringing The King of Trash to audiences across the country. The documentary was also selected for the 2026 Red Rock Film Festival in Utah.

From the Fall of Saigon to a New Beginning in America

The documentary begins in April 1975, when the Duong family lost its paper-recycling business in South Vietnam following the fall of Saigon. David Duong's father, Jim Thu Tai Duong, was known in Vietnam as Vua Rac, or "the King of Trash," the name that inspired the film's title. According to the family account presented in the documentary, 23 relatives escaped Vietnam aboard a small boat. Interviews, archival footage and reenactments filmed in Vietnam recount the family's departure and the perilous journey that followed.

"We almost died out there in the ocean. We had only one choice: survive," David Duong says in the documentary.

The family spent time in a refugee camp in the Philippines before reaching the United States in 1979. In San Francisco, more than a dozen relatives shared apartments in the Tenderloin. Younger family members attended school during the day, while relatives collected bottles, cardboard and paper, sometimes working at night. The work drew on the recycling trade the family had known in Vietnam, but they also had to learn a new language and find work and customers in an unfamiliar city.

Jim Thu Tai Duong taught his family that nothing useful, and no person with potential, should be thrown away. "There is honor in every kind of honest work," he told his family.

David Duong's years in San Francisco included discrimination and the difficulties of entering business as an immigrant. The film recounts those experiences through David Duong's own account and examines how they influenced his decision to establish a company of his own. The business grew from the family's knowledge of recycling and years spent earning a living from recovered materials.

David Duong's Journey to Building California Waste Solutions

In 1992, David Duong founded California Waste Solutions in Oakland, beginning with used trucks. The company expanded from recovered-materials work into recycling collection, processing and material recovery for residential, commercial and municipal customers. According to company figures, California Waste Solutions serves more than 343,000 customers in Oakland and San Jose and operates several Bay Area recycling facilities.

The documentary traces David Duong's journey from collecting recyclables alongside his family on the streets of San Francisco to building California Waste Solutions into a major recycling and environmental services company. It also examines the years of hard work, discrimination, business challenges and family responsibilities that shaped his career, showing how the experience of starting over as refugees in America became the foundation for his success as an entrepreneur.

Decades after fleeing Vietnam, the family returned to develop environmental services operations near Ho Chi Minh City. Through Vietnam Waste Solutions, California Waste Solutions developed large-scale waste-treatment infrastructure, including the Da Phuoc Integrated Solid Waste Facility. According to the company, the facility handles roughly half of Ho Chi Minh City's waste.

The return also brought the family's history full circle. The family that left the country following the war later became involved in developing waste-management infrastructure there, linking David Duong's work in California with the recycling business his father had established in Vietnam.

The documentary includes younger family members Victor Duong and Kristina Duong, whose perspectives appear alongside those of relatives who remember the escape from Vietnam and the first years of resettlement in America. Together, their accounts show how the family's past continues to shape the next generation and its role in the businesses.

The Duong Family's Journey Through Generations

Director Errol Webber was a cinematographer on the Academy Award-winning documentary short Music by Prudence. For The King of Trash, Webber combined family interviews, historical footage and reenactments shot in Vietnam. Webber has described the film as "a portrait of hope rising from loss, of a family who turned pain into purpose and created light from what others left behind."

The film moves between the events of 1975, the family's arrival in San Francisco, David Duong's career and the environmental services operations established in Vietnam. It also includes accounts from relatives who lived through displacement and from family members born or raised after resettlement in the United States.

San Francisco Film Festival and Upcoming Digital Release

The King of Trash will be represented at the 13th San Francisco International New Concept Film Festival's red carpet and awards ceremony on Sunday, November 1, 2026, at the historic Herbst Theatre, 401 Van Ness Avenue, San Francisco. The ceremony is scheduled from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m., with David Duong and director Errol Webber expected to attend. The festival's selected-film screening program runs from October 25 through October 31. For event details and attendance inquiries, contact sfncff.rsvp@gmail.com or visit the festival's official website.

Following 12 screening events across the United States and its recognition at film festivals, The King of Trash is preparing to reach a wider audience. The production team is working to finalize digital distribution through Amazon and other streaming platforms, allowing viewers beyond the original screening locations to discover the Duong family's history and David Duong's journey as a Vietnamese refugee and American entrepreneur. Further details, including participating platforms and release dates, will be announced once distribution arrangements are confirmed.

About California Waste Solutions

Founded in 1992 by David Duong, California Waste Solutions provides recycling collection, processing, customer service, and material recovery for residential, commercial, and municipal customers in Northern California, including Oakland and San José. Through its subsidiary Vietnam Waste Solutions, the company also operates large-scale environmental infrastructure in Ho Chi Minh City. Headquarters: 1211 Embarcadero, Suite 300, Oakland, CA 94606. www.calwaste.com.

About Vietnam Waste Solutions

Vietnam Waste Solutions is the wholly owned Vietnamese subsidiary of California Waste Solutions and operator of the Da Phuoc Integrated Solid Waste Facility serving Ho Chi Minh City. Da Phuoc Integrated Solid Waste Facility (DPI) was developed as Vietnam's first sanitary landfill modeled on U.S. Subtitle D standards. Existing operations include sanitary landfill management, recycling and material recovery, composting, leachate and wastewater treatment, treated-water reuse, landfill-gas collection and electricity generation. VWS is advancing the proposed 50- to 60-megawatt Da Phuoc waste-to-energy project and continues development of the Long An Green Environmental Technology Park. Company website: www.vnwaste.com.

releases.title: From Prison Classroom to National Audience: "Basement People" Screens at San Quentin Film Festival and Digitally Debuts Nationally on Securus Technologies Tablets
releases.body:
Directed by Christine Swanson and winner of Best Short Film at the Martha's Vineyard African American Film Festival, Kyale Akeem Williams' Academy Award-eligible film is now available to incarcerated viewers nationwide

PLANO, Texas, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Basement People, an Academy Award-eligible short film written by incarcerated screenwriter Kyale Akeem Williams and directed by award-winning filmmaker Christine Swanson, screens at the 2026 San Quentin Film Festival. Technology access inside correctional facilities carried the film from a Michigan prison classroom to the festival circuit and secure tablets nationwide, extending education beyond the classroom, sustaining creative collaboration, and building the connection, skills, and sense of purpose essential to rehabilitation.

On October 22, 2026, Securus Technologies, a technology company that equips more than 1,800 correctional agencies with a comprehensive portfolio of connectivity solutions that enhance public safety and optimize facility operations, made Basement People available to incarcerated viewers through the Securus Media Store. Delivered across Securus' network of more than 550,000 secure tablets in corrections facilities nationwide, the release expands access to meaningful content that can spark reflection, reinforce learning, and bring to life where education and creative work can lead in rehabilitation and reentry.

Williams developed the screenplay through a Calvin Prison Initiative screenwriting course at Michigan's Richard A. Handlon Correctional Facility. Recognizing the strength of his work, Calvin University professor Geert Heetebrij connected Williams with Swanson, a fellow Detroiter who went on to direct the film. Through JPay accounts on the Securus platform, Williams stayed connected with Swanson and the project's broader support network, allowing them to continue developing the screenplay during his incarceration and turn classroom learning into sustained creative collaboration.

"When I first read the script, I was struck by its emotional precision, moral ambiguity, and relatable characters," said Swanson, whose directing credits include The Clark Sisters: First Ladies of Gospel and Albany Road. "It did not ask for pity. It asked for understanding. Now, people inside may see their own families reflected in it, and that means a great deal to me."

The film follows Tina, a seven-year-old girl who retreats to her family's basement after a traumatic incident and finds refuge with her uncle Keith, whom the family has dismissed and isolated. Their bond creates safety without judgment and illustrates how empathy and connection can interrupt cycles of neglect and harm.

"I wrote Basement People to explore how vulnerable family members respond to familial violence, emotional abuse, and mental health conditions," said Williams. "I hope this interpersonal complexity will encourage audiences to sympathize with the protagonist without dehumanizing her tough and aggressive family. After all, each family member is a victim in their own way—someone who also deserves love, mercy, and compassion."

After winning Best Short Film at the Martha's Vineyard African American Film Festival, Basement People earned Academy Award eligibility. Its screening at the San Quentin Film Festival, now in its third year and the first film festival established inside a U.S. prison, brings a screenplay developed inside one correctional facility to an audience inside another, proving how education, creative opportunity, and technology access can carry work beyond institutional walls.

"Access to technology while incarcerated gives individuals an opportunity to discover and develop abilities they may never have had the chance to explore," said Jessica Lust, Chief Product Officer, Securus Technologies. "In particular, secure tablets create connectivity to educational tools, mentors, and collaborators that lead to skill building, motivation, and purpose, which can be the foundations of rehabilitation and successful reentry."

"Our responsibility extends beyond providing services. It includes listening to the communities where we operate and supporting the local people and organizations that understand what their communities need to thrive," said Shamia Lodge, Stakeholder Engagement Director, Securus Technologies. "When we pair their insight with resources that expand access and opportunity, we help create conditions in which more individuals can build lasting success."

About Securus Technologies

Securus Technologies, an Aventiv company and the industry leader, equips more than 1,800 correctional agencies with a comprehensive portfolio of technology solutions that enhance public safety and optimize facility operations. Securus helps agencies bring communications, intelligence, mobility, education, monitoring, and operational visibility together in one integrated ecosystem that improves safety, efficiency, and outcomes. Through purpose-built infrastructure, extensive corrections expertise, and continuous investment in innovation, Securus helps agencies modernize how corrections work while supporting successful reentry and stronger communities.

About Basement People

Basement People explores the impact of trauma poverty, and untreated mental illness on children and urban communities. Through Tina, a sensitive young girl, and her uncle Keith, a man isolated by his own struggles, the film reveals how cycles of neglect and violence can be interrupted by empathy and understanding.

Written by Kyale Akeem Williams, an incarcerated writer at Michigan's Richard A. Handlon Correctional Facility through the Calvin Prison Initiative and directed by award-winning filmmaker Christine Swanson, Basement People unites two artists whose shared roots ground the film in authenticity. This collaboration bridges art, justice and community healing while amplifying Detroit's creative legacy.

releases.title: GRUNGE: The Noise is Coming Back!
releases.body:
TUCSON, Ariz., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GRUNGE is a feature-length suspense horror-thriller born from the collision between Seattle's grunge Legacy and the underground music culture, mythology, and psychedelic horror.

Set in 1993, the story focuses on a popular grunge band.  But it isn't a nostalgic recreation of the 1990s. Rather, it's a horror film using the mythology of grunge as its cultural foundation. The film combines the raw energy of the grunge music culture with a genuinely terrifying set of circumstances ... something simultaneously familiar and dangerous—a story rooted in recognizable cultural history that gets pushed into psychedelic, psychological, and visceral horror.

A rising rock band is on the verge of stardom, with a scorching new single lighting up the airwaves and their debut music video premiering on MTV. Everything seems to be falling into place, when disaster strikes. Following a sudden and tragic turn of events, the band is thrust into a violent psychedelic spiral, leading them down a blood-soaked path of death and destruction,

Based on a story by Rene Rivas with special effects by Quin Davis, the 15-minute short film premieres on Crypt TV on Halloween Eve, October 30, 2026. (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8pcHB-sEGvc).  The goal of this 'proof of concept' short version is to ignite audience interest, turning that audience into a community that will help bring the full feature version to life. 

Rene Rivas is an independent filmmaker, writer, producer, director, and cinematographer based in Tucson, Arizona, who has spent years developing independent narrative and genre projects, with a particular interest in creating ambitious films outside the traditional studio system.

Quin Davis is a sought-after Special FX expert whose work has appeared in productions by major studios, including Paramount, Sony, Universal, and Columbia.  His company, Davis FX, is also based in Tucson.  

The film will be shot in Tucson in March 2027.

An official Indiegogo campaign for the GRUNGE feature film will launch when the short film premiers on Crypt TV.  The coordinated release gives audiences an immediate opportunity to watch the proof of concept, experience the world of the film, and participate directly in helping create the feature. The film already has in-kind services partnership with Movie Maker Magazine. For an independently financed feature, that is significant.

Launching a feature-film crowdfunding campaign in conjunction with Crypt TV is a first-of-its-kind collaboration – a direct bridge between a short-form proof of concept and a feature-film campaign.  The strategy is designed to create a single, concentrated moment in which the film's release and its next stage of development become one event.

One of the project's most significant music-world connections comes through Daniel House, whose history is deeply intertwined with the Seattle scene that gave birth to grunge. House was a central figure behind C/Z Records, the influential Seattle label that released early recordings from artists who would become foundational figures in the grunge movement, including Nirvana, Soundgarden, and Green River, among others. His involvement gives GRUNGE a connection to the actual musical history behind the mythology. 

This isn't a film simply using grunge as an aesthetic. GRUNGE is also receiving support from Sub Pop, the legendary Seattle-based label whose history is inseparable from the emergence of grunge into the international cultural consciousness.  The relationship further connects the project to the musical ecosystem that helped define the genre. Together, the involvement of C/Z Records and Sub Pop gives GRUNGE something particularly valuable: AUTHENTICITY.
